topic: Library Classes Arrays and String Handling

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a wrapper class in Java?
questions.explanation: String is a regular Java class for text, whereas Wrapper classes (like Character, Boolean, Double) strictly wrap primitive data types.

questions.question: What will be the output of: System.out.println("Java".substring(1, 3));
questions.explanation: Extracts from index 1 ('a') up to index 2 ('v'). Index 3 is excluded.

questions.question: Identify the error: char c = (char) 65.5;
options: Cannot cast a decimal to a char
questions.explanation: 65.5 will be truncated to 65 during the explicit cast, and ASCII 65 is 'A'.

questions.question: In a double dimensional array, how are elements stored in memory conceptually?
questions.explanation: A double dimensional array represents data in a tabular format, conceptually structured as rows and columns.

questions.question: What will "apple".compareTo("Apple") return?
questions.explanation: It returns the ASCII difference. 'a' (97) - 'A' (65) = 32, which is a positive value.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to append text to the end of a StringBuffer?
questions.explanation: StringBuffer uses the append() method to add new characters to the end of the buffer sequence.

questions.question: What happens when an object of a wrapper class is assigned back to its corresponding primitive variable?
questions.explanation: Converting an object of a wrapper class into its corresponding primitive data type is known as Unboxing.

questions.question: What will be the output of: System.out.println(Character.toUpperCase('5'));
questions.explanation: If the given character is not a letter, toUpperCase() simply returns the original character.

questions.question: What will be the output of: int a[] = new int[3]; System.out.println(a[1]);
questions.explanation: When an integer array is instantiated, all elements are automatically initialized to the default value of 0.

questions.question: What will be the output of: System.out.println("Board".indexOf('z'));
questions.explanation: If a character is not found in the string, the indexOf() method returns -1.

questions.question: What will be the output of: StringBuffer sb = new StringBuffer("TCS"); System.out.println(sb.length());
questions.explanation: The length() method for StringBuffer returns the number of characters currently present in the buffer.

questions.question: Identify the error: int arr[] = {1, 2, 3}; arr[0] = 5.5;
options: Cannot assign a double to an int array
questions.answer: Cannot assign a double to an int array
questions.explanation: An int array can only hold integers. Attempting to assign the decimal 5.5 results in a lossy conversion error.

questions.question: Identify the error: String text = Integer.toString(25);
options: toString() is not a method of Integer
questions.explanation: Integer.toString(int) is the correct static method to convert an integer primitive into a String.

questions.question: Identify the error: boolean b = "Cat".equalsignorecase("cat");
options: String literals cannot invoke methods directly
questions.explanation: Java methods are strictly case-sensitive and must follow camelCase conventions.

questions.question: Identify the error: StringBuffer sb = new StringBuffer("Hello"); sb.setCharAt("H", 'M');
options: The first argument must be an integer index
The second argument must be a String
questions.answer: The first argument must be an integer index
questions.explanation: The setCharAt(int index, char ch) method requires the position (integer) as the first argument, not a String.
